## Quickstart

Make your first API call in a few minutes. Every plan includes API access, and the Free plan includes 30 calls a month.

1. Sign in to Consensus

Create a free account or sign in at consensus.app. The dashboard in the next step only opens when you're signed in.

2. Open the API & MCP Dashboard

Go to consensus.app/api-mcp. You can also get there from your profile icon: choose API & MCP Dashboard.

3. Create and copy an API key

Click Create API key, name the key, and click Copy API key. The full key is shown only once, so store it somewhere safe.

Already have a key? Open Keys and clients and click New key.

4. Make your first request

Save the key in an environment variable named `CONSENSUS_API_KEY`:

```bash
export CONSENSUS_API_KEY="paste-your-key-here"

```

Then search. `query` is the only required parameter, and the key goes in the `x-api-key` header.

```bash
curl "https://api.consensus.app/v1/search?query=creatine%20and%20cognitive%20function" \
  -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY"

```

```python
import os
import requests

resp = requests.get(
    "https://api.consensus.app/v1/search",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["CONSENSUS_API_KEY"]},
    params={"query": "creatine and cognitive function"},
)
resp.raise_for_status()

for paper in resp.json()["results"]:
    print(paper["title"], "—", paper["journal_name"], paper["publish_year"])

```

## Base URL and authentication

All requests go to:

```
https://api.consensus.app

```

Every request must include your API key in the `x-api-key` header:

```http
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY

```

See plans and access for each plan's monthly calls, page sizes, features, and rate limits.

highlights:
# API plans and access

> What each Consensus plan includes on the API: monthly calls, papers per request, pagination, full-text excerpts, complete text, citations, and rate limits.

The API is self-serve on every Consensus plan. Your plan sets how many calls you get each month, how many papers each request can return, and which features you can use.

## Get a key

1. Open the dashboard

Sign in to Consensus and go to consensus.app/api-mcp, or click your profile icon and choose API & MCP Dashboard.

2. Create a key

Click Create API key, name it, and copy it. If you already have a key, open Keys and clients and click New key. The full key is shown once.

3. Send it on every request

Pass the key in the `x-api-key` header. Requests without a valid key return `401`.

## What each plan includes

|  | Free | Pro | Teams | Deep | Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Included calls per month | 30 | 500 | 500 | 2,000 | Custom |

...

## Errors

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | Missing, invalid, or revoked key | Check the `x-api-key` header, or create a new key |

...

## Enterprise

Enterprise adds custom call volumes and rate limits and up to 1,000 papers per request. An Enterprise contract covers search only: complete text, citations and references, and Threads are billed per credit at the standard rate, on top of the contract. Enterprise keys authenticate the same way as every other key: send them in the `x-api-key` header on requests to `api.consensus.app`.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> `Authorization: Bearer` is for the MCP server (`mcp.consensus.app/mcp`), not the REST API. See MCP API key access.

For Enterprise access, contact sales. Setting Consensus up behind an AI gateway or in Microsoft 365 Copilot? See the Enterprise guides.

auth.title: Connection reference
highlights:
# Connection reference

> The technical facts every integration needs: the MCP endpoint, transport behavior, both authentication options, OAuth discovery documents, and the domains to allowlist.

Everything on this page applies to any MCP client or gateway. The platform guides link back here rather than repeating it.

## Endpoint and transport

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| MCP endpoint | `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Responses | Buffered JSON. There is no SSE endpoint and the server never returns SSE event streams. |
| Sessions | Stateless. No `Mcp-Session-Id`, no session affinity, so your gateway needs no sticky-session configuration. |
| Tools | `search`, plus the thread tools `create_thread`, `get_thread`, `add_to_thread`, and `find_threads` for signed-in accounts and API keys, and `get_full_text` for paid plans. See the tool reference. |

> [!WARNING]
> 
> All MCP and JSON-RPC calls must target the `/mcp` path. The bare host `https://mcp.consensus.app/` only answers health checks and OAuth discovery.

Where a product lets you choose a transport, pick Streamable HTTP explicitly. Some gateways default to SSE, which will fail against this server.

## Authentication

Two options. For a shared, server-side gateway credential, use an API key.

> [tab] API key (recommended for gateways)
> 
> A single opaque credential sent as a bearer token:
> 
> ```http theme={null}
> Authorization: Bearer ak_live_...
> 
> ```
> 
> It lives entirely server-side, involves no user redirect and no token refresh, and maps to your Enterprise tier. Generate one from your Consensus account: profile icon → API & MCP Dashboard → Keys and clients → New key. The full key is shown once.
> 
> Treat it like a password: keep it out of client-side code, public repositories, and screenshots.

> [tab] OAuth 2.0 (per-user)
> 
> Authorization-code flow only. There is no client-credentials grant, so OAuth always involves a per-user consent step; each user signs in to their own Consensus account.
> 
> |  |  |
> | --- | --- |
> | Authorization URL | `https://consensus.app/oauth/authorize/` |
> | Token URL | `https://consensus.app/oauth/token/` |
> | Dynamic Client Registration | `https://consensus.app/oauth/register/` (RFC 7591) |
> | Scope | `search`. Request `scope=search` or omit it; it's the default. This is not an OIDC provider, so there are no `openid` or `email` scopes. |
> | PKCE | Required. `S256` only; requests without a `code_challenge` are rejected. |
> 
> Keep the trailing slashes on the URLs.
> 
> Dynamic Client Registration issues public clients: a `client_id` with no `client_secret`, which is why PKCE is required. If your gateway needs a confidential client (a `client_id` and `client_secret` pair) and can't do DCR, Consensus provisions those manually for enterprise partners. Contact sales and we'll set one up.

## Discovery documents

Gateways that support automatic configuration can read these:

- `https://mcp.consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` — points to the authorization server
- `https://consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` — full metadata: endpoints, scopes, and `S256`

## Firewall allowlist

If your organization runs an egress firewall, allow these hosts. Per-host wildcards cover any path changes on our end (new discovery documents, versioned endpoints) without another change request, while staying scoped to the hosts this integration touches:

```text
mcp.consensus.app/*
consensus.app/*
clerk.consensus.app/*

```

`clerk.consensus.app` is our authentication provider. Sign-in does a browser redirect through it, so it needs to be reachable wherever your users complete the consent screen. If you use the API-key path only, users never sign in and this host isn't needed.

> [accordion] Tighter scope: exact URLs
> 
> If policy requires exact URLs rather than wildcards, allow these. Expect a new change request any time we add or change a path.
> 
> ```text theme={null}
> https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp                                  MCP JSON-RPC endpoint
> https://mcp.consensus.app/                                     health check
> https://mcp.consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
> https://consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
> https://consensus.app/oauth/register/
> https://consensus.app/oauth/authorize/
> https://consensus.app/oauth/token/
> https://clerk.consensus.app/*                                  sign-in redirects
> 
> ```

auth.title: The Consensus API
highlights:
Written by Allison Elechko

October 12, 2026

...

The Consensus API lets you integrate Consensus search directly into your own applications, tools, and workflows. Use it to programmatically search academic research and retrieve relevant papers without needing to run each search manually in Consensus.

API access is available directly from your Consensus account. Your API usage and Consensus MCP usage share the same monthly pool of calls. The number of calls included each month depends on your subscription tier.

For full technical documentation, endpoints, parameters, and response details, read our API docs here.

---

# How to create an API key

You can create and manage API keys from the API & MCP Dashboard.

1. Click your profile icon (bottom-left corner)
2. Select API & MCP Dashboard
3. Open the ' Keys and Clients' tab
4. Click ' New key'
5. Give your API key a name so you can identify what you're using it for
6. Create the key and copy it somewhere secure

Your full API key is only shown once. Make sure you copy it when you create it.

If you lose an API key, you won't be able to view it again. Instead, revoke the existing key and create a new one.

---

# Make your first API request

Once you've created an API key, you can use it to authenticate requests to the Consensus API.

To make a search request, you'll need three things:

1. The Consensus search endpoint: `https://api.consensus.app/v1/search`
2. Your API key, passed in the `x-api-key` request header
3. A `query` parameter containing what you want to search for

For example, if you want to search for research on whether creatine improves muscle strength, your request would send that question as the `query` to the Consensus search endpoint.

If you're using a tool such as Postman, a programming language, or another application to make the request, add your Consensus API key as an `x-api-key` header.

The API also supports filters that can help narrow your research, including publication date, study type, sample size, citation count, journal, academic field, country, open-access status, and more.

For request examples and a full list of available parameters and responses, see the Consensus API Reference.

---

...

# How to manage your API keys and MCP clients

The Keys and Clients tab is where you manage both your API keys and MCP connections.

- API keys: you can create and revoke API keys
- MCP clients: you can connect Consensus to supported clients such as ChatGPT or Claude. If you've already connected a client, you'll see it here.

...

# Common API errors

| API Error message | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 - `Invalid authentication credentials` | The API key is incorrect, revoked, or isn't being sent using the required header. | Confirm you're using the correct API key in the `x-api-key` header. If you've lost the key, revoke it in the API & MCP Dashboard and create a new one. |

...

# Keep your API key secure

Treat your API key like a password.

Don't share it publicly or include it in publicly accessible client-side code, public repositories, screenshots, or other places where someone else could access it.

If you believe a key has been exposed, revoke it from the API & MCP Dashboard and create a new one.

You can manage your API keys, monitor API and MCP usage, review billing, and change your additional usage settings at any time from the API & MCP Dashboard.

---

auth.title: Add a citable evidence layer to an agent you already ship
highlights:
## Wiring it in

```bash
# OAuth per user, so each person's own plan and limits apply
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp

```

```bash
# one service key, full control over pagination
curl -G "https://api.consensus.app/v1/search" \
  -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "query=your agent's search string"

```

Choose by auth model rather than by preference: MCP when each user should search under their own account and limits, REST when the integration needs one shared quota and programmatic pagination.

gate.title: API plans and access
highlights:
# API plans and access

> What each Consensus plan includes on the API: monthly calls, papers per request, pagination, full-text excerpts, complete text, citations, and rate limits.

The API is self-serve on every Consensus plan. Your plan sets how many calls you get each month, how many papers each request can return, and which features you can use.

## Get a key

1. Open the dashboard

Sign in to Consensus and go to consensus.app/api-mcp, or click your profile icon and choose API & MCP Dashboard.

2. Create a key

Click Create API key, name it, and copy it. If you already have a key, open Keys and clients and click New key. The full key is shown once.

3. Send it on every request

Pass the key in the `x-api-key` header. Requests without a valid key return `401`.

## What each plan includes

|  | Free | Pro | Teams | Deep | Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Included calls per month | 30 | 500 | 500 | 2,000 | Custom |
| Max calls with additional usage | 30 | 1,000 | 1,000 | 10,000 | Custom |
| Max papers per request (`page_size`) | 20 | 300 | 300 | 750 | 1,000 |
| Pagination past the first page | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Full-text excerpts | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Complete text of open-access papers** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Institutional full-text links (`institutional_access_url`)* | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Citations and references (beta)*** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Rate limit | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | Custom |

* Returned on the first 50 search results and on Thread citations when you've selected your institution in Consensus settings. An organization key uses the institution of the person who created it.

** `GET /v1/papers/full_text`, at 1 credit per paper returned.

*** `GET /v1beta/papers/citations` and `GET /v1beta/papers/references`, at 1 credit per 100 papers returned. Both are in beta, so their request and response schemas may change in the coming days.

Every plan can use every search filter. Compare plans at consensus.app/pricing.

## How calls are counted

- One call per 100 papers returned, rounded up, with a minimum of one call per request. A request that returns 20 papers is 1 call; 150 papers is 2 calls.
- A Thread is charged by the amount of work the agent does. `mode` controls the effort: a `deep` run does more work than a `pro` run, so it costs more. A failed run costs nothing. While a Thread runs, its maximum possible cost counts as used. If that doesn't fit under your plan's limit, creating the Thread or adding a follow-up returns `429`.
- One credit per full text returned. Complete text costs 1 credit for each paper whose Markdown comes back, and a credit counts the same as a call. Papers that come back blocked or not found cost nothing. A paper charged to you in the last 24 hours, through the API or MCP, normally comes back free.
- One credit per 100 citing or cited papers returned. `GET /v1beta/papers/citations` and `GET /v1beta/papers/references` are charged by the papers on the page, rounded up, with a minimum of 1 credit per request.
- API and MCP share one monthly pool. Searches from your API key and from your MCP connection draw down the same allowance.
- Usage resets on the 1st of each month. Track it in the Usage tab of the API & MCP Dashboard.

### Additional usage

Pro, Teams, and Deep can keep making calls past the included amount, up to the plan's maximum, at $0.05 per call. Additional usage is off by default; turn it on in the API & MCP Dashboard. Free plans stop at 30 calls.

## Page size and pagination

- `page_size` defaults to 20. A larger value is capped to your plan's maximum rather than rejected, so check the `page_size` echoed in the response.
- Pages are zero-indexed. Requesting `page=1` or later needs a paid plan; on Free it returns `403`.
- A query returns at most 1,000 results in total. `(page + 1) × page_size` can't exceed 1,000 on any plan. With `page_size=250`, pages 0–3 cover the full 1,000. To go wider, split the topic into narrower queries or tighter filters.

## Rate limits

Every self-serve plan allows one request per second per account. A faster request returns `429` with a `retry-after` header; wait that long and retry. Enterprise accounts can have custom limits.

The Threads endpoints follow the same one-request-per-second limit, except `GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}`, which allows up to three requests per second. That limit is shared across all of your account's Threads. While a Thread is running, poll it every `poll_after_seconds`: 5 seconds for `pro`, 20 for `deep`.

`GET /v1/papers/full_text`, `GET /v1beta/papers/citations`, and `GET /v1beta/papers/references` each allow one request per second on every plan, Enterprise included.

...

## Enterprise

Enterprise adds custom call volumes and rate limits and up to 1,000 papers per request. An Enterprise contract covers search only: complete text, citations and references, and Threads are billed per credit at the standard rate, on top of the contract. Enterprise keys authenticate the same way as every other key: send them in the `x-api-key` header on requests to `api.consensus.app`.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> `Authorization: Bearer` is for the MCP server (`mcp.consensus.app/mcp`), not the REST API. See MCP API key access.

For Enterprise access, contact sales. Setting Consensus up behind an AI gateway or in Microsoft 365 Copilot? See the Enterprise guides.

API access is available directly from your Consensus account. Your API usage and Consensus MCP usage share the same monthly pool of calls. The number of calls included each month depends on your subscription tier.

For full technical documentation, endpoints, parameters, and response details, read our API docs here.

---

# How to create an API key

You can create and manage API keys from the API & MCP Dashboard.

1. Click your profile icon (bottom-left corner)
2. Select API & MCP Dashboard
3. Open the ' Keys and Clients' tab
4. Click ' New key'
5. Give your API key a name so you can identify what you're using it for
6. Create the key and copy it somewhere secure

Your full API key is only shown once. Make sure you copy it when you create it.

If you lose an API key, you won't be able to view it again. Instead, revoke the existing key and create a new one.

---

# Make your first API request

Once you've created an API key, you can use it to authenticate requests to the Consensus API.

To make a search request, you'll need three things:

1. The Consensus search endpoint: `https://api.consensus.app/v1/search`
2. Your API key, passed in the `x-api-key` request header
3. A `query` parameter containing what you want to search for

For example, if you want to search for research on whether creatine improves muscle strength, your request would send that question as the `query` to the Consensus search endpoint.

If you're using a tool such as Postman, a programming language, or another application to make the request, add your Consensus API key as an `x-api-key` header.

...

# How calls are counted

API searches return up to 20 papers by default. You can use the `page_size` parameter to request more papers per page.

Each call covers up to 100 papers:

- 1-100 papers = 1 call
- 101-200 papers = 2 calls
- 201-300 papers = 3 calls
- And so on, with each additional 100 papers counting as another call

More advanced actions, such as creating a Consensus Thread, running a Pro or Deep Thread, or adding follow-up questions to a Thread, may use more calls depending on the amount of work required.

Thread usage is variable because Consensus may run multiple research steps, search across more papers, read and synthesize results, and generate a cited response.

You can view your usage from your profile > API & MCP Dashboard. The Usage tab shows activity by platform and tool, including searches, created Threads, Pro Threads, and Deep Threads.

---

# API and MCP usage limits

API and MCP usage share one monthly pool of calls.

| Plan | Included calls per month | Maximum calls with additional usage ($0.05/call) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | 30 | 30 (no additional usage) |
| Pro | 500 | 1,000 |
| Team | 500 | 1,000 |
| Enterprise | 500 | 1,000 |
| Deep | 2,000 | 10,000 |

Additional usage costs $0.05 per call after you've used the calls included in your plan.

Your usage resets on the 1st of each month.

---

The Keys and Clients tab is where you manage both your API keys and MCP connections.

- API keys: you can create and revoke API keys
- MCP clients: you can connect Consensus to supported clients such as ChatGPT or Claude. If you've already connected a client, you'll see it here.

...

# How to enable additional usage

Additional usage lets paid users continue making API and MCP calls after using all of the calls included in their plan.

Additional usage is turned off by default.

To enable it:

1. Open the API & MCP Dashboard
2. Select the settings control in the upper-right corner
3. Under API & MCP settings, turn on Enable additional usage
4. Save your changes

Once enabled, calls beyond your plan's included amount are billed at $0.05 per call, up to your plan's maximum monthly call limit.

You can turn additional usage off at any time. If you turn it off after you've already exceeded your included calls, you won't be able to make any more API or MCP calls until your usage resets. You'll still be billed for any additional calls made before you turned additional usage off.

Free users cannot enable additional usage. To access additional usage, upgrade to a paid plan.

---

Don't share it publicly or include it in publicly accessible client-side code, public repositories, screenshots, or other places where someone else could access it.

highlights:
# Start building with the Consensus API and MCP

> Pick a surface, run your first filtered search, and find the guide for what you are building.

Four steps from zero to a working integration.

1. Pick your surface

Use MCP to try Consensus inside Claude or ChatGPT in two minutes, or when each person should search under their own account. Use the API for anything in code — monitoring agents, literature tables, pipelines, and scientific agents running on one shared key.

2. Run one filtered search

Make your first request, then add filters one at a time. The filters are where precision comes from.

```bash
curl -G "https://api.consensus.app/v1/search" -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "query=vision-language models for robot manipulation" \
  --data-urlencode "domain=cs" \
  --data-urlencode "year_min=2024"

```

3. Read the guide for what you are building

Start with internal tools or research systems, then read best practices for rate limits, pagination, and grounding rules.

4. Scale up when you need to

Enterprise adds up to 1,000 results per request, custom call volumes, and custom rate limits. Talk to us about a trial.

| --- | --- |
| `search` | Find ranked, peer-reviewed papers for a query in one call. |
| `get_full_text` | Read the complete text of open-access papers from search results or Threads, as Markdown. |
| `create_thread` | Start a Thread: hand a research question to the Consensus research agent. |
| `get_thread` | Poll a Thread and read the agent's cited answer. |
| `add_to_thread` | Ask a follow-up in an existing Thread. |
| `find_threads` | List your Threads and find an earlier one. |

`search` works without an account. The thread tools need a signed-in Consensus account or an API key. `get_full_text` needs a paid plan.

> [card] Quick start: Search & Threads
> 
> When to use search, when to start a Thread, and how a Thread runs.

...

## Security

- Endpoint: Only connect to the official URL: `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`
- API keys: Store securely using environment variables. Never share keys in prompts or public conversations. Rotate if compromised.
- Data handling: Search queries are sent to the Consensus API over HTTPS/TLS. Results contain publicly available academic paper metadata. No personal data is stored from MCP requests.

...

> [card] MCP Specification
> 
> Learn more about the Model Context Protocol.

mcp.title: Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp
highlights:
# Consensus MCP Server: Scientific Literature Search for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor

[!Website](https://consensus.app)
[!Docs](https://docs.consensus.app/consensus-mcp)
[!Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
[!Follow on X](https://x.com/ConsensusNLP)

The official Consensus MCP server gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Perplexity and any other MCP client semantic search over **400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers and all of PubMed**. Your assistant can find research papers, filter them by study design and journal quality, and give answers that cite real studies, without leaving the chat.

It's a hosted remote server, so there's nothing to install. Connect, ask a research question, and get back ranked papers with DOIs, citation counts, study type, sample size and a one-line takeaway.

**Server URL**

```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

## Why use the Consensus MCP server

- **One index for all of science.** Biomedical, clinical, psychology, computer science, economics, materials and every other field. The index includes all of PubMed and is updated weekly.
- **Semantic search, not keyword matching.** Results are ranked by how well they answer the question, so "does creatine help memory in older adults" works as written. No Boolean strings or MeSH terms needed.
- **Evidence-quality filters.** Limit results to RCTs, meta-analyses or systematic reviews (19 study types), human or controlled studies, a minimum sample size, top-quartile journals (SJR), recent years, clinical guidelines, or Medical mode (about 8M papers from the top 1,000 medical journals).
- **Full text, not just abstracts.** Licensed full text from publisher partners plus open-access full text. On paid plans, results can include the passages that answer your query.
- **A research agent when one search isn't enough.** Threads hand a question to the Consensus research agent, which searches, reads papers and writes a cited answer you can follow up on.
- **Safe for enterprise and pharma.** SOC 2 Type II. Customer data is not used to train AI models, no personal data is stored from MCP requests, and enterprise agreements can include zero data retention. See Security and data handling.

...

## Tools

Your assistant picks the right tool for the question.

| Tool | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `search` | Find ranked, peer-reviewed papers for a query in one call. Works without an account. |
| `create_thread` | Hand a research question to the Consensus research agent. |
| `get_thread` | Poll a Thread and read the agent's cited answer. |
| `add_to_thread` | Ask a follow-up in an existing Thread. |
| `find_threads` | List your Threads and find an earlier one. |

`search` returns title, authors, journal, year, DOI, citation count, study type, sample size, a key takeaway and a link to the paper. Its filters cover publication date, study design (RCT, meta-analysis, systematic review, cohort study and more), human and controlled studies, minimum sample size, journal quality (SJR quartile), minimum citations, open access, preprints, clinical guidelines, Medical mode, academic field and country of study.

The Thread tools need a Consensus account or an API key. See when to use search and when to start a Thread.

highlights:
# Connection reference

> The technical facts every integration needs: the MCP endpoint, transport behavior, both authentication options, OAuth discovery documents, and the domains to allowlist.

Everything on this page applies to any MCP client or gateway. The platform guides link back here rather than repeating it.

## Endpoint and transport

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| MCP endpoint | `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Responses | Buffered JSON. There is no SSE endpoint and the server never returns SSE event streams. |
| Sessions | Stateless. No `Mcp-Session-Id`, no session affinity, so your gateway needs no sticky-session configuration. |
| Tools | `search`, plus the thread tools `create_thread`, `get_thread`, `add_to_thread`, and `find_threads` for signed-in accounts and API keys, and `get_full_text` for paid plans. See the tool reference. |

> [!WARNING]
> 
> All MCP and JSON-RPC calls must target the `/mcp` path. The bare host `https://mcp.consensus.app/` only answers health checks and OAuth discovery.

Where a product lets you choose a transport, pick Streamable HTTP explicitly. Some gateways default to SSE, which will fail against this server.

## Authentication

Two options. For a shared, server-side gateway credential, use an API key.

> [tab] API key (recommended for gateways)
> 
> A single opaque credential sent as a bearer token:
> 
> ```http theme={null}
> Authorization: Bearer ak_live_...
> 
> ```
> 
> It lives entirely server-side, involves no user redirect and no token refresh, and maps to your Enterprise tier. Generate one from your Consensus account: profile icon → API & MCP Dashboard → Keys and clients → New key. The full key is shown once.
> 
> Treat it like a password: keep it out of client-side code, public repositories, and screenshots.

> [tab] OAuth 2.0 (per-user)
> 
> Authorization-code flow only. There is no client-credentials grant, so OAuth always involves a per-user consent step; each user signs in to their own Consensus account.
> 
> |  |  |
> | --- | --- |
> | Authorization URL | `https://consensus.app/oauth/authorize/` |
> | Token URL | `https://consensus.app/oauth/token/` |
> | Dynamic Client Registration | `https://consensus.app/oauth/register/` (RFC 7591) |
> | Scope | `search`. Request `scope=search` or omit it; it's the default. This is not an OIDC provider, so there are no `openid` or `email` scopes. |
> | PKCE | Required. `S256` only; requests without a `code_challenge` are rejected. |
> 
> Keep the trailing slashes on the URLs.
> 
> Dynamic Client Registration issues public clients: a `client_id` with no `client_secret`, which is why PKCE is required. If your gateway needs a confidential client (a `client_id` and `client_secret` pair) and can't do DCR, Consensus provisions those manually for enterprise partners. Contact sales and we'll set one up.

...

## Protocol version

The server tracks the current MCP specification. Some gateways refuse upstream servers below a minimum protocol version (Kong and Azure API Management require `2025-06-18` or later). If your gateway reports a version mismatch, contact us with the version it requires.

mcp.title: Quick start: Search & Threads
highlights:
# Quick start: Search & Threads

> The two ways an assistant uses Consensus MCP: search for ranked papers in one call, or hand a research question to the Consensus research agent with Threads.

Consensus MCP gives your assistant two ways to work with the literature:

- Search: the `search` tool returns ranked papers in one call. Your assistant reads them and writes the answer.
- Threads: the thread tools hand the whole research question to the Consensus research agent. The agent searches, reads the papers, and writes a cited answer. Your assistant starts the Thread, waits for it, and shows the result.

Ask your question in plain language and your assistant picks the right tool for it. To make it use a specific one, say so in your prompt: for example, "Search Consensus for…" for search, or "Start a Consensus research thread on…" for a Thread.

## Search vs Threads

|  | Search | Threads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tools | `search`, then `get_full_text` to read open-access papers in full | `create_thread`, `get_thread`, `add_to_thread`, `find_threads` |
| Your assistant gets back | Ranked papers with abstracts and metadata | A written analysis with inline citations, grounding quotes, and the cited papers |
| Functionality | Semantic paper search with filters | Search, citation crawls, author search, finding specific papers, reading full papers, searching attached papers and collections, and saving papers to your Library |
| Steps per request | One | Many |
| Timing | Seconds | Minutes. The assistant polls until the answer is ready |
| Follow-ups | Each call stands alone | Follow-ups build on the earlier answers in the same Thread |
| Account | Works without an account at reduced limits | Requires a signed-in Consensus account or API key |

Need a quick lookup, or papers for your assistant to reason over? Use search. Need a researched, cited answer to a question that takes several steps? Use a Thread.

### MCP Server
Endpoint: https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp

The Model Context Protocol server is the recommended surface for any LLM client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT, in-house agents). It exposes the same primitives as the REST API as MCP tools. OAuth-based authentication, dynamic client registration, streaming-friendly. Designed to be added to a host with a single configuration entry.
